profilePeriod: Chancellorship, 1982–1998; later disclosure of the period’s donations scandal retained as context.

sources.title: Kohl: subsidiarity, family and humane technological progress
sources.evidence: Advocates local and Land autonomy, delegated European competences, family support and individual responsibility; couples social-market welfare with scientific progress subject to human dignity. Nuclear safety and protection against genetic manipulation are explicit. Defends NATO and conscription alongside arms reduction.

sources.title: Bundestag: Kohl retrospective and donations
sources.evidence: Documents parliamentary election as chancellor in 1982, repeated electoral contests and defeat in 1998, negotiated reunification, Maastricht, and the 1999 revelations of unreported donations and refusal to identify donors.

sources.title: bpb: 1998 acoustic surveillance amendment
sources.evidence: The governing CDU/CSU-FDP coalition with SPD support amended Article 13 in January 1998 to allow acoustic surveillance of homes for serious criminal investigations; civil-liberties objections remained significant.

sources.title: Bundestag: unity as a task, 1990–1994
sources.evidence: Kohl government pursued equal living conditions after reunification, constitutional changes on asylum, gender equality and environmental protection. Asylum restrictions coexist with national reconstruction and constitutional government.

sources.title: Bundestag asylum amendment debate
sources.evidence: Primary parliamentary record of the cross-party asylum compromise and safe-third-country restrictions; evidence for government-era restriction, not a claim that every speaker expresses Kohl personally.

sources.title: Kohl: Munich Security Conference
sources.evidence: Supports NATO collective defence and Bosnia peace deployment, careful enlargement with attention to Russia and Ukraine, European defence cooperation and deeper political integration; denounces revival of old nationalism.

sources.title: Kohl: Catholic gathering and Europe
sources.evidence: Presents Christian faith as a public moral source and defends state responsibility toward unborn life; combines that with reconciliation, freedom and Western alliances.

sources.title: bpb: repeal of Paragraph 175
sources.evidence: Paragraph 175 was abolished in 1994 during Kohl government. Traditional marriage preferences cannot be equated to blanket criminalisation of homosexuality.

sources.title: Kohl economic and fiscal policy, Reimut Zohlnhöfer
sources.evidence: Tax cuts, deregulation, Treuhand privatisations and Lufthansa sale; Telekom partial privatisation from 1996. Reform was gradual and institutionally constrained, with major reunification spending and continued welfare commitments.

sources.title: Kohl: defence of independent Bundesbank
sources.evidence: Explicitly praises legally guaranteed central-bank independence and monetary stability as foundations for a free economy.

sources.title: White House: Clinton and Kohl press availability
sources.evidence: Kohl endorses successful GATT completion, European union alongside Atlantic ties, science exchanges, support for Russian reform and efforts toward peace in Bosnia.

sources.title: Kohl social policy history
sources.evidence: Fiscal restraint and welfare retrenchment coexist with preservation of social insurance and introduction of long-term care insurance in 1995.

sources.title: Kohl bibliography
sources.evidence: Lists Ich wollte Deutschlands Einheit, represented by Kai Diekmann and Ralf Georg Reuth, Berlin 1996; distinguishes later 1998 paperback and French translation. Also lists Kohl memoir volumes.

sources.title: CVCE: Kohl political memoir excerpt
sources.evidence: Search-index record identifies Kohl memoir of European negotiations on German unity, Propyläen-Verlag 1996, with Diekmann/Reuth assistance. Full page returned tool error; corroboration used from bibliography.

sources.title: Kohl: scientific progress and ethical limits
sources.evidence: Speech on technological progress and ethical limits; evidence supplements the directly read 1986 discussion of research, nuclear safety and human dignity.

facts: In 1986 Kohl explicitly advocated subsidiarity for municipalities, Länder, federal government and European institutions.
Reunification used a federal constitutional framework with national solidarity.
estrutura.tension: Federalism is not secession; equal living conditions and European competences limit local autonomy.

facts: Parliament elected Kohl in 1982, elections confirmed him and the 1998 election ended his government.
Donations from his governing years were concealed, and he later refused to identify donors.
representacao.tension: Democratic institutions coexist with patronage and deficient financial accountability; do not turn those failings into support for dictatorship.

facts: The 1998 governing coalition backed expanded residential surveillance against organised crime.
His public framework remained the democratic rule of law.
poder.tension: Security powers are subject to law; surveillance support does not imply death penalty, arbitrary detention or unlimited executive censorship.

facts: The 1993 government-backed asylum compromise restricted entry through safe third countries.
Kohl defended national cultural belonging alongside European openness.
imigracao.tension: Restrictive asylum and integration preferences do not mean racial exclusion or compulsory erasure of private cultural traditions.

facts: In 1996 Kohl supported NATO collective defence, its Bosnia mission and European military capacity.
His 1986 speech defended conscription while seeking East-West balance with fewer weapons.
diplomacia.tension: Armed deterrence and alliance obligations coexist with negotiated peace and opposition to aggressive nationalism.

facts: Kohl supported international peace deployments, Russian reform assistance and deeper European institutions.
He expressly rejected return to the old sovereign nationalist state.
intervencao.tension: He rejects isolationism and unilateral national supremacy alike; allied intervention does not mean imperial domination of neighbours.

facts: Government privatised Lufthansa, Treuhand assets and part of Telekom.
It preserved social insurance and added long-term care insurance in 1995.
economia.tension: Private enterprise and property with a social safety net; neither nationalisation of all strategic sectors nor privatisation of police/courts.

facts: Tax reductions and liberalisation remained policy aims amid reunification costs.
In August 1991 Kohl explicitly defended Bundesbank independence and monetary stability.
controle.tension: Market allocation with social and legal regulation, rather than either a command economy or unregulated private money.

facts: At the March 1993 White House press conference Kohl sought successful GATT completion.
European economic integration was central to his government.
comercio.tension: Trade liberalisation through negotiated institutions; does not require abolishing all safeguards overnight.

facts: His 1991 Catholic address treated faith and protection of unborn life as politically relevant.
In 1986 he explicitly criticised costs of secularisation while supporting constitutional democracy.
religiao.tension: Christian democratic public ethics differs from clerical government or exclusion of nonbelievers.

facts: He publicly defended unborn life in 1991 and traditional family support in 1986.
His government era included the 1994 repeal of the criminal provision against male homosexuality.
moral.tension: Traditional family norms do not justify assuming all consensual adult relationships should be criminalised; working mothers were acknowledged.

facts: In 1986 he defended research, industry and modern medicine while insisting on nuclear safety and limits on human genetic manipulation.
His government period included environmental constitutional protection.
tecnologia.tension: Technological optimism is bounded by environmental stewardship and Christian bioethics, not transhumanist acceleration.

limitations: Historical persona, not current German CDU policy. Later private positions excluded; later evidence of governing-period donations retained.

Digital surveillance, AI, cryptocurrency, gender identity, Brazilian quotas and Amazon mining require analogical judgments; no direct Kohl statement claimed. N reserved for real balanced preferences, not undocumented topics.

Coalition legislation is evidence of governing practice but does not establish Kohl personally endorsed every detail. Foundation sources have a CDU affiliation and are cross-checked with Bundestag, bpb and White House records.
Original CVCE book page failed to open; its indexed bibliographic record was corroborated by the Kohl bibliography. No Brazilian or English full-edition translation verified; use original title.

recommendedMetadata.reason: Current PT and EN description, name and role accurately summarise the preserved chancellorship period and fit limits.

bookDecision.reason: Authored political memoir of reunification, especially relevant to defining political achievement. Kohl is the memoir voice; Kai Diekmann and Ralf Georg Reuth are credited as presenting/editing collaborators. First edition 1996 confirmed; later paperback is not first publication. No verified PT-BR or English book edition found, so retain German original in both fields. Existing books catalog has no Kohl entry.
